clue.text: Millions impatient to meet giant

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)
agog means eagerly impatient, all excited

explanation.surface: Someone who has made millions can hardly wait to meet a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: In British legend Gog and Magog are giants, guardians of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend and the Bible this figure is one of a pair of giants, so the name stands for a giant.

clue.text: Very keen old commander's transport to island

parts.note: mad about something means very keen on it
an aga was an Ottoman commander; with the 's this gives AGAS
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic old officer has his vehicle taken across to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The large island state off the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: In dropping pressure, struggle to breathe air

indicators.note: dropping means a letter is let fall from the word before it

parts.note: to gasp is to struggle for breath
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone struggles for breath as the cabin pressure drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes P (pressure) from GASP; 'In' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air, empty talk, is called gas, and air itself is a gas.

clue.text: Unctuous, when former foreign minister's about

indicators.note: about means the minister's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Sir Edward Grey was British Foreign Secretary 1905-16
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: A smarmy manner is noticed whenever an old foreign secretary is around.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' joining Grey to 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous and greasy both describe oily, ingratiating manners.

clue.text: Church musicians, say, who agitated for reform

parts.note: musicians are an example of artists, as 'say' signals

explanation.surface: Church musicians are cast as campaigners for change.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a 19th-century British working-class movement demanding votes for all men.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chartist movement campaigned for the People's Charter, a programme of parliamentary reform.

clue.text: Flower girl appearing in pantomime

definitions.meaning: a garden flower, also called aquilegia
the sweetheart of Harlequin in the traditional harlequinade

explanation.surface: A flower girl turns up in a Christmas show.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a plant with spurred petals and Harlequin's beloved in the harlequinade.

clue.text: Cut top off less leafy tree

indicators.note: cutting the top off a down entry removes its first letter

parts.note: balder means more bare, less covered with leaves

explanation.surface: Someone lops the top off a thinning tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree of the birch family common by rivers.

clue.text: Artist 'captured a horse, typical uneven : Gauguin 'subject

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads "Artist 'captured a horse, typical uneven : Gauguin 'subject": TITIAN round A + H is clear, but 'typical uneven' is OCR garble and the definition cannot be recovered.
annotationWithheld.clue: Artist 'captured a horse, typical uneven : Gauguin 'subject

clue.text: Back great deal, being, aware of future potential?

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
a sight, as in 'a sight better', means a great deal

explanation.surface: Someone backs a big deal, feeling they can tell what the future holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Clairvoyance, the supposed power of foreseeing events, is the gift meant.

clue.text: Writer heard to be 'full of bitter irony.

indicators.note: heard means the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: sarky is British slang for sarcastic, full of bitter irony

explanation.surface: A writer is said to be biting and sarcastic.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, sarky and the pen-name sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-name of H. H. Munro, the Edwardian short-story author.

clue.text: Drove away from' fell that holds charm

indicators.note: holds means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to fall in battle is to die, so fell gives died
a charm is a magic spell

explanation.surface: Someone was chased off a hillside fell that had an enchantment on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the hill but is the past tense of fall, died.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or scatter, as with doubts or a crowd.

clue.text: Uninspired writer holding first of essays to get mark above a C

indicators.note: holding means the writer word wraps round the extra letter

parts.note: a hack is a writer of dull, routine work

indicators.note: first of selects the opening letter of essays

explanation.surface: A dull writer fits in an essay to scrape up a mark over a C grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mark above a C' suggests a grade but means the diacritic in Czech č.
explanation.definitionFit: This inverted circumflex is the accent placed over letters such as c in Czech.

clue.text: Charitable helper offers posses-girl

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Charitable helper offers posses-girl': 'posses-girl' is garbled OCR and the wordplay for the rest of the letters cannot be recovered.

clue.text: Made impossible to' see do again in bold letters

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
letters says the word bold is used as raw letters to be rearranged

parts.note: to iterate is to do again

explanation.surface: Something is printed over in heavy type until it can no longer be read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' is an unusual anagram signal: the word bold is treated as loose letters to be shuffled before the other piece goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliterated means wiped out or blotted from view.

clue.text: Bright as one whose views are of: unrestricted general import

definitions.text: Bright as one whose views are of: unrestricted general import

parts.words: Bright as one whose views are of: unrestricted general import
parts.note: John Bright, the Victorian radical, campaigned for imports without tariffs; the clue reads like an abstract praise of broad-minded views

explanation.surface: A clever thinker whose ideas have wide significance.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bright and Richard Cobden led the Anti-Corn Law League for open commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A person advocating commerce without tariffs or quotas, as Bright did.

clue.text: In Oxford, something beneath an upper second in Spanish — come, on!

definitions.text: In Oxford, something beneath an upper

parts.note: olé is the Spanish cry of encouragement, like 'come on!'

explanation.surface: An Oxford student with an upper second degree hears a Spanish cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' and 'upper second' suggest the university degree, but an Oxford is a lace-up shoe with an upper above its base.
explanation.definitionFit: The underside of a shoe lies beneath its upper, the part covering the foot.

clue.text: His criminal activities. set tongues going

definitions.text: His criminal activities. set tongues going

parts.words: His criminal activities. set tongues going
parts.note: reads as gossip about a crook, but the tongues are tongues of flame started by an arsonist

explanation.surface: A villain's misdeeds get everyone gossiping.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for an arsonist, whose crime makes flames leap up.

clue.text: Secreting directly into blood, new drug upset timeless principle

indicators.note: upset in a down entry turns the two letters before it upside down

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: timeless means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a doctrine is a principle or tenet

explanation.surface: A fresh drug overturns a long-held medical principle about secretions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NE into EN; 'timeless' takes T out of DOCTRINE to leave DOCRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ductless glands release hormones straight into the bloodstream, which is what the term describes.

clue.text: Comfortable fit — daughter can get in as well

parts.note: fit and well both mean healthy

indicators.note: get in means the daughter letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: too means as well, also

explanation.surface: A healthy daughter manages to get in as well.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside TOO to make TODO.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfortable in the sense of financially secure, prosperous.

clue.text: Prepared a table, but not competent to take cash

indicators.note: but not means the following word's letters are taken away from table

parts.note: competent means able
the ready is British slang for ready money, cash

explanation.surface: Someone lays a table but proves useless at taking the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being poised and fully ready for use or action.

clue.text: Terrifying man wanting bloodshed — love to go to the front

indicators.note: to go to the front says one letter shifts to the start of the word

parts.note: gore is blood shed in violence
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A frightening man craves violence, with love put first.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving O to the front of GORE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster of folk tales, a man-eating giant who terrifies all.

clue.text: Bone from old Persian king whose top half is dug up

indicators.text: whose top half is dug up
indicators.note: in a down entry, dug up means the top half of the king's name is turned upward

parts.note: Darius was the name of several ancient Persian kings

explanation.surface: A bone comes from the tomb of an ancient Persian king, half dug up.
explanation.walkthrough: Only DAR, the first three of six letters, is turned, giving RAD + IUS.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two forearm bones, alongside the ulna.

clue.text: Ride continually up and down and wave to ship

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy sea wave
a coaster is a ship trading along a coast

explanation.surface: Someone bobs up and down at sea and waves to a passing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground ride whose cars swoop steeply up and down along a track.

clue.text: Queen's less wager with husband its a girl!

indicators.note: less means the following pieces are subtracted from the queen's name

parts.note: Elizabeth is the name of two English queens
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: After a royal birth, the Queen loses a bet with her husband: it's a girl!
explanation.walkthrough: ELIZABETH less BET and H leaves the shorter name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, a short form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Shady, dealer turned up kings *and queens?

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: kings and queens are examples of VIPs, very important persons

explanation.surface: A dodgy trader appears among royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a flashy petty crook trading in black-market goods.

clue.text: The animal to shoot at first

indicators.note: at first says the shooting word comes before to

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game

explanation.surface: A hunter decides to take a shot at the animal first.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-moving tree-dwelling primate of West Africa.

clue.text: Began dietitian's new formula

indicators.note: a new formula means the letters of dietitian are rearranged into a different form

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A nutritionist launched a new diet formula.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiated means set going, started.

clue.text: Obligation to' secure equal outcome

definitions.meaning: a binding duty or restricting commitment
to fasten with a knot or cord

explanation.surface: A duty to make sure the match ends level.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a bond, to fasten, and a draw.

clue.text: Off TV I do finally store copy here

definitions.text: Off TV I do finally store copy here

indicators.note: off means the letters are spoilt and thrown into disorder
finally takes the last letter of store

parts.note: to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Someone records programmes off the TV and keeps the copy on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges TV, I, DO and the final E of store; the whole clue also describes what the answer is used for.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic tape on which television programmes can be recorded and stored.

clue.text: Piece of wood fitted with blade at end?

definitions.text: Piece of wood fitted with blade at end?

parts.words: Piece of wood fitted with blade at end?
parts.note: suggests a carpentry tool, but describes a long wooden shaft with a pointed metal head, a weapon

explanation.surface: A wooden handle with a cutting edge attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrusting or throwing weapon, a wooden shaft tipped with a blade.
